BUSINESS IT SERVICES

Backup and disaster recovery planning.

Backup and disaster recovery planning defines how business information and systems can be recovered after a failure. HeyDock can help scope backup configuration, restore testing and recovery documentation. The agreed service should identify what is protected, where copies are held and who acts when recovery is needed.

Discuss requirementsExplore services

SERVICE EXPLAINED

What does this service involve?

A backup job reporting success does not establish that an entire business service can be recovered. Recovery depends on usable data, application configuration, access, dependencies and available infrastructure. Planning should therefore connect technical backups to the actual order in which your team needs services restored.

The engagement starts by identifying the business outcome, existing responsibilities and the changes you authorise. HeyDock then confirms suitable delivery capacity, the working window and the evidence needed to complete the task. Related licences, hardware, subscriptions and specialist services are included only where the proposal says so.

PRACTICAL SCOPE

What can be included?

The final statement of work identifies the tasks that apply to your environment.

Protection scope

List systems, data sources and retention requirements. Identify cloud services that may need a separate backup arrangement, and record ownership of backup subscriptions and administrative access.

Restore tests

Choose representative files or workloads, restore them into an appropriate environment and check usability. Record the test result, elapsed time, gaps and the person responsible for corrective action.

Recovery runbooks

Define the recovery sequence, decision-makers and communications. Agree recovery-time and recovery-point objectives with the business before treating them as service commitments.

EXAMPLE REQUIREMENT

How a project might work.

A company replacing its file server can include a restore test before migration and a recovery checkpoint before cutover. This connects the migration plan to a tested fallback rather than relying only on the existence of a backup.

PLANNING AND COST

What affects the scope and price?

Cost depends on the number of users, devices or sites; technical complexity; access requirements; delivery hours; travel; and the work needed before and after implementation. Provide relevant system versions and existing supplier responsibilities so the quotation can distinguish labour from licences, equipment and recurring charges.

For a well-defined task, a visit or project quotation may be appropriate. Where important dependencies are unknown, a paid assessment can produce a better implementation scope. Any response, attendance or recovery target must be explicitly agreed; requesting a service does not create an immediate support commitment.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Backup and disaster recovery planning FAQs

Does backup guarantee no data loss?+

No. Recovery depends on the protection design, backup frequency, failures and tested restore capability. Objectives and limitations must be agreed.

Can you review existing backups?+

An assessment can review coverage, access, retention, restore evidence and gaps, subject to authorised access.

What information should we include in an enquiry?+

Describe the objective, location, affected systems, preferred timing and existing support arrangements. Do not send passwords or sensitive business records in the enquiry form.
